subject: anatomy
title: Embryology of the gut tube and diaphragm development

steps.tx: The primitive **gut tube** derives from endoderm following lateral and cephalocaudal embryonic folding. It is partitioned into three anatomical regions supplied by three unpaired ventral aortic branches: the foregut supplied by the celiac trunk, the midgut supplied by the superior mesenteric artery, and the hindgut supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery. The junction between foregut and midgut lies at the major duodenal papilla.

steps.tx: The **midgut rotation** is an intricate embryological sequence occurring between the sixth and tenth gestational weeks. Rapid elongation causes physiological herniation into the umbilical cord. The midgut rotates two hundred and seventy degrees counterclockwise around the axis of the superior mesenteric artery. The cephalic limb returns first on the left, followed by the cecal bud on the right. Incomplete rotation predisposes to volvulus.

The midgut rotates two hundred and seventy degrees counterclockwise around the superior mesenteric artery. Incomplete rotation predisposes to midgut volvulus.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of midgut development: rapid elongation at week 6 pushes loops into the umbilical cord, the loop rotates 90 degrees anticlockwise around the superior mesenteric artery while herniated, returns by week 10 with a further 180 degrees, giving 270 degrees in total, then fixes.
vis.caption: The midgut turns 270 degrees anticlockwise around the superior mesenteric artery; failures give omphalocele, malrotation and volvulus.

steps.tx: Four embryonic structures fuse to form the **muscular diaphragm**. The septum transversum forms the central tendon. The two pleuroperitoneal membranes close the pericardioperitoneal canals. Dorsal mesentery of the esophagus forms the bilateral diaphragmatic crura. Ingrowth from the lateral body walls forms the peripheral muscular rim. Motor innervation is delivered exclusively by the phrenic nerve from cervical levels three, four and five.
steps.say: Four embryonic structures fuse to form the muscular diaphragm. The septum transversum forms the central tendon. The pleuroperitoneal membranes close the pericardioperitoneal canals. Dorsal mesentery of the esophagus forms the crura. Lateral body wall ingrowth forms the peripheral rim. Innervation is delivered by the phrenic nerve from C3, C4 and C5.

left.title: Septum transversum
points: Carries phrenic nerve as it descends

right.title: Pleuroperitoneal membranes
points: Failure of left membrane causes Bochdalek hernia
Defect allows abdominal viscera into thorax

steps.tx: Failure of pleuroperitoneal membrane closure causes **congenital diaphragmatic hernia**, occurring ninety percent of the time on the left side through the posterolateral pleuroperitoneal canal of Bochdalek. Abdominal contents herniate into the hemithorax during critical fetal bronchial branching, causing severe bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia and persistent pulmonary hypertension. Morgagni hernia is an anterior retrosternal defect, which is far rarer and typically benign.
